conventions: Predicative LAMED before a predicate noun: where a written verb already carries the predication - HAYAH taking the English copula (11.6 *be our chief*, 11.8 *thou shalt be our head*, 11.9 *shall I be your head*) or SIM writing it as a bare object complement (11.11 *made him head and chief*, both LAMEDs) - the resultative LAMED is its own `unrepresented` unit and the predicate noun keeps only its own word. Rule 49's resultative frame reaches a LAMED only where no verb is written to carry the copula, and rule 21's ruling covers the passive recasting; this chapter's shape is neither. A dative LAMED standing beside it whose suffix the ASV recasts as a possessive determiner is unrepresented on the same terms, the suffix taking the determiner under rules 18 and 40.

A particle standing inside an English verb phrase was tested by rule 44's subtraction against the bare English verb the ASV chose, not against the Hebrew stem. *turned again* (11.8), *bring home again* (11.9), *go back* (11.35), *took away* (11.13, 11.15), *drive out* (11.7), *went around* (11.18), *gathered together* (11.20), *passed over* (11.29, 11.32), *came out* (11.34), *offer it up* (11.31), *go down* (11.37) and *sent away* (11.38) all keep their particles, the bare verb not writing the whole lexeme. The *again* of *restore ... again* (11.13) is `added`: *restore* is *cause to return* entire, so nothing is left for the word to complete, exactly as rule 44 leaves the *back* of hiphil BO -> *bring him back*.

Bare nominals after verbs of motion. BO takes no direct object in this chapter, so the supplied *to* before MINNIT (11.33) and HA-MITSPAH (11.34) is rule 33's word for a terminative place accusative and belongs to the name, headed there under rules 24 and 31. AVAR is the other case: 11.29 writes it twice with ET-marked objects and once with a bare one, so the *unto* before *the children of Ammon* is the preposition the English verb's valency needs to reach its own object and belongs to the verb under rule 44. Read which the Hebrew noun is, as rule 44's own closing limit directs.

An appositional *even* was placed by what stands immediately after it. Before a bare nominal that no object marker and no conjunction stands on it is `added` (11.33, before *twenty cities*). Before a written preposition it is that preposition's expansion and the pair goes whole to it, headed on the relational word (11.36, MIN -> *even on*); rule 16 names *even unto*, *even to*, *even till*, *even for* and *even as*, and this chapter reads *even on* on the same terms, since the rule states the condition rather than a list. Where a conjunction morpheme stands before the preposition, rule 16's count gives the waw the bare *even* and the preposition the relational word alone (11.13, 11.22).
report: Checked all 75 candidate lemma groups plus the full verse dump end to end. No cross-verse split found: every difference the table surfaces is the ASV writing something different, and the source licenses each one.

Prepositional fusion is consistent. MI-PNEI fuses at 11.3 (*from*) and 11.33 (*before*) and splits at 11.23 and 11.24 (*from before*); LI-PNEI fuses at 11.9 and 11.11; LI-QRAT splits at 11.31 and 11.34. That is rule 30's one-rendering condition doing what it says, not two analyses of one construction.

The *even* family resolves four ways on what stands after the word, which is rule 16's own triage: a waw immediately before a limit preposition takes the bare *even* while AD takes *unto* (11.13, 11.22); a MIN with no conjunction beside it keeps *even on* whole (11.36); an AD whose waw the ASV left unrendered takes *until* alone (11.33); and an *even* standing before a bare nominal that no marker and no conjunction stands on is `added` (11.33).

The closest thing to a split is SHUV with a particle. 11.8 *turned again*, 11.9 *bring home again* and 11.35 *go back* fold the particle in; 11.13 marks *again* `added`. Rule 44's subtraction runs against the bare English verb the ASV chose, and *restore* writes hiphil SHUV entire where *turn*, *bring* and *go* do not - one test, four answers. The neighbouring *took away* at 11.13 and 11.15 stays folded because *take* alone does not write the deprivation, which is rule 44's own SUR -> *take away* neighbourhood. Recorded as a convention.

BO with a place accusative takes the supplied *to* on the noun (11.33, 11.34, rule 33); AVAR reaches its bare object through the verb's *unto* (11.29, rule 44), and that same verse writes AVAR twice with ET-marked objects, which is what licenses the difference. Recorded as a convention.

Also checked clean: the HAYAH frame's *that* (11.4, 11.35, 11.39 to the apodosis waw; 11.5 kept inside the frame under rule 45's rider); LAMED before infinitives, including the unrepresented one at 11.35 after a modal; AL after BAKHAH, unrepresented at both 11.37 and 11.38; the demonstrative phrases at 11.21, 11.26 and 11.37, all giving the one written determiner to the pronoun and leaving both articles unrepresented; and the five `added` units, each of which answers to no morpheme in its clause.

BSB: no genuine error. The R x 20, C x 7, To x 7 and Td x 7 bulk, and the paragogic he and nun at 11.6, 11.13 and 11.18, are the documented convention difference under rules 32 and 40 - BSB attaches function morphemes to their host words. 11.20's directive he is unrepresented because the BET already took the English, which rule 32's own closing sentence provides for. The two substantive candidates, 11.14 YOSEF and 11.31 ASHER/YETSE, are genuine ties already named in those verses' notes under rule 8.

One edge left alone and worth recording: 11.35 heads the fused *cannot* on YAKHOL while 11.10 heads the fused *surely* on the negative. Rule 23's negation sentence would pull the first onto LO, but its examples are all negation plus a function morpheme and YAKHOL is a lexical verb, so the two are different constructions and the verse names the competing head. Not changed.

No promotions. The OD/YASAF tie at 11.14 and the pleonastic-particle case at 11.13 are each a single occurrence, and the corpus tables supplied cover neither SHUV, YASAF nor LAQAH, so a rule written from them could not be checked against the precedent the briefing requires.
